title: Fritto Misto
subtitle: Mixed fried seafood Italian style
excerpt: A classic Italian mixed fry of prawns and cod in a light crumb coating, served with lemon wedges and parsley. The key is very hot oil and working in small batches so the coating crisps rather than steams.
sourceNotes: Fritto misto is a beloved tradition along the Italian coastline, particularly in Liguria, the Veneto, and across the south. The mix of fish and seafood varies by what the boats bring in; this version uses widely available prawns and cod as a practical home version.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The seafood can be coated up to 30 minutes ahead and kept on a tray in the fridge. Fry just before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil should reach 180C before frying. Use a probe thermometer.

content.text: The three-stage coating of flour, egg, then panko breadcrumbs gives a crisper, lighter result than a thick batter. Pat the seafood completely dry before coating; any moisture will make the crumb steam instead of fry. Never crowd the pan: cook in batches of four to five pieces and let the oil return to temperature between each batch.
Pat all the seafood completely dry with kitchen paper. Set up three shallow bowls: seasoned flour in the first, beaten egg in the second, and panko in the third.
Coat each piece of seafood in flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in egg, then roll in panko. Set aside on a clean tray.
Pour the oil into the frying pan to a depth of about 2cm. Heat over a medium-high heat until it reaches 180C on a probe thermometer.
Fry in small batches of 4 to 5 pieces for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deeply golden and cooked through. Lift out onto a wire rack or kitchen paper. Season with salt immediately.
Allow the oil to return to 180C before adding the next batch.
Scatter the parsley over the finished fritto misto and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

items.symptom: Crumb is falling off during frying.
items.cause: Seafood was damp, or the crumb was not pressed on firmly.
items.fix: Pat seafood dry and press the panko coating on firmly.

items.cause: Oil was not hot enough, or the pan was overcrowded.
items.fix: Check oil temperature is 180C; fry in small batches only.

items.symptom: Prawns have curled into tight balls.
items.cause: They cooked too quickly in very hot oil.
items.fix: Score the underside of larger prawns to keep them straighter.
